## Applicable behaviour

For the integration represented by this workspace (Palimpsest ⇄ Ordarium, pinned at **v1.3.1**), the observation cursor — the state change-feed cursor in `StateChangeFeed.changes()` / `StateChangePage.cursor` — is a **single global, filter-independent durable position** over the whole ledger's commit-observation order (`ordarium_state_changes.change_seq`). A `namespace` filter narrows which changes are returned but does **not** re-base or partition the cursor: the cursor is always the global commit position, and the same cursor resumes the global scan. A cursor beyond the ledger's global high-water mark fails closed with `InvalidCursorError`. This applies — **not** the "per-subscription" reading.

## Why (source-precedence decision)

The governing rule is `docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md` (PLMP-ALN-2):

1. **Rule 1 — the published contract of the exact pinned version governs.**
   - Pin confirmed in `package.json` + `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: `@ordarium/core`, `@ordarium/ledger-sqlite`, `@ordarium/host-kit` at `ordarium-v1.3.1`, with `@ordarium/testing` 1.3.1; installed `node_modules/@ordarium/*/package.json` all report `1.3.1`.
   - Shipped type declarations (`@ordarium/core` `types.d.ts`): `StateChangePage.cursor` is documented as the *"Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change"*; `StateChangeFilter.namespace` *"Restrict observation to one namespace; absent observes every namespace"*; the feed is the *"Additive observation capability over the state kind"* that reads *"after a durable position."* That is the observation cursor, and it is declared filter-independent.
   - Shipped implementation (`@ordarium/ledger-sqlite` `index.js`): *"the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence"* (ORD-BOOT-0.1), validated against `MAX(change_seq)` over the whole table; the index is `(namespace, change_seq)` and is used only as a filter. `MemoryLedger` mirrors this: positions are one contiguous global `1..n`, filter applied during the walk, and `after > length` throws `InvalidCursorError`.
2. **Rule 3 — informational records never override 1 or 2.** The only source claiming per-subscription is `docs/engineering/notes/cursor-note.md`. It self-declares *"informational, not normative,"* states it *"was not updated against the current pinned artifact,"* and attributes the reading to *"an earlier Ordarium line."* It is also unreferenced anywhere in the repo. It is therefore a stale explanatory record, void as authority on this interface — not a competing contract.
3. **Rule 2 — no conflict from the project normatives.** Palimpsest's normative SDS and specs 17/19/23/35 define different, project-internal cursors (`graph.project.cursor` = canonical event position; `viewCursor`; projection cursor). Those co-apply to other propositions and say nothing that re-scopes the Ordarium observation cursor.
4. **No "subscription" concept exists in the pinned artifact** (zero occurrences), so the per-subscription reading is not even representable in the current pinned interface; the only scoping knob, `filter.namespace`, narrows results without rebasing the cursor.

Corroborating context: the repo has advanced to the 1.3.1 pin while the alignment charter's revision log (`docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md`) still describes 1.2.0 — documents lag the pinned artifact here, which is exactly the situation rule 1 is written for.

## Scope / honesty

This is the contract that governs the pinned Ordarium interface. In the current workspace Palimpsest does not itself consume `changes()`; the telemetry externalization (`src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts`) uses `StateStore.list` pagination (`nextCursor`) and CAS writes, a distinct surface. So the global/filter-independent semantics apply to the pinned integration and bind whenever the change feed is consumed; they are not currently exercised by Palimpsest code.

## Decision

The observation-cursor behaviour that applies is the **pinned v1.3.1 published contract: one global, filter-independent durable position** — resolved locally under PLMP-ALN-2 rule 1 (shipped declarations + implementation), with the contrary note void under rule 3. No load-bearing conflict remains that the Ordarium peer owns, so no boundary escalation is warranted.
